name: Sequence
edition: Sequence instruction sheet, no year printed

source.title: Sequence game instructions, copy hosted on a retailer CDN

setup.text: Place the board flat with room for the draw deck, chips and each player's discards. Use the 104 cards; jokers are not used.
With two players or teams use blue and green chips. Red chips are used only when there is a third player or team.
Teams must be even: two teams of equal size, or three teams of equal size. Team members sit alternately with opponents (every third seat with three teams) and share one chip colour.
Players cut cards and the lowest (aces high) deals. Shuffle and deal every player the same number of cards.
The player left of the dealer goes first. Play is clockwise.

turn.summary: Play a card from your hand, put a chip on a matching space, then draw.
steps: Choose a card from your hand and place it face up on your own discard pile.
Put one of your chips on a free board space showing that card. Each card is on the board twice, so either space will do.
Draw a replacement card before the next player takes their turn.
A two-eyed jack is wild: put a chip on any open space. A one-eyed jack removes one opposing chip from the board, and you cannot place on that space this turn.

end: The game ends as soon as one player or team makes the required number of sequences. The corner spaces count as your chip.

scoring.text: A sequence is five of your chips in a connected line, across, up and down, or diagonally. A corner counts as a chip for everyone, so a sequence using a corner needs only four of your chips.
Two sides: first to make two sequences wins. Three sides: first to make one sequence wins.
In the two-sequence game, the second sequence may share one space with the first.

missed.text: You cannot remove a chip that is already part of a completed sequence.
A dead card (both board spaces covered) can be swapped: discard it, say so and take a new card, once per turn, then play normally.
If you do not draw before the next player has played and drawn, you lose the right and must play on with fewer cards.
No table talk or coaching teammates. If it happens, each member of that team must discard a card of their choice.
If the draw deck runs out, shuffle all the discard piles to make a new deck.
Jacks do not appear on the board.

unverified: Publisher name (Goliath / Pressman) is taken from the host of the copy; the sheet text names no publisher. No age or year is printed in the text, so the age is left as reference only.
